problem: Investor has a grievance against a SEBI-regulated entity (listed company, registered intermediary, or market infrastructure institution) and needs to know how to escalate it through SCORES and, if needed, ODR.
user_intent: File a SCORES complaint and understand what happens at each stage, including what to do if unsatisfied.
eligibility: Complaint concerns securities-market matters governed by the SEBI Act 1992, SCRA 1956, Depositories Act 1996, or relevant Companies Act 2013 provisions administered by SEBI.
Complaint is against a listed company, a SEBI-registered intermediary, or a market infrastructure institution.
Complaint is lodged within 1 year of the date of the cause of action (SEBI may reject complaints filed later).
preconditions: Complainant has Name, Address, Email, PAN (or PEKRN if PAN-exempt), Mobile Number, and Date of Birth ready — these are mandatory to register on SCORES.
Ideally, the investor has already raised the issue with the entity directly (SCORES is a facilitation/escalation layer, not necessarily the first stop).

step_by_step_process.action: Register on scores.sebi.gov.in via 'Sign in/Sign up', either by fetching KYC details from the KRA database (enter PAN + DOB, OTP-verify mobile) or by filling the registration form manually.

Sign in (via User ID, registered mobile, or registered email + OTP + password) and click 'Lodge a complaint'; choose the correct category/sub-category (up to 5 sub-categories against the same entity) and attach supporting documents (jpg/jpeg/pdf, up to 10 files, 20MB cumulative).

Complaint is auto-forwarded to the concerned Entity and simultaneously to the relevant Designated Body (e.g. an exchange). Entity must resolve and upload an Action Taken Report (ATR) within 21 calendar days.
If unsatisfied with the ATR, request a review within 15 calendar days of the ATR date. If the entity misses the 21-day deadline, escalation to first-level review is automatic either way.
First-level review: the Designated Body (e.g. exchange) takes up the matter with the entity and must submit its own ATR within 10 calendar days.
If still unsatisfied, request a second-level review within 15 calendar days of that ATR (or it escalates automatically if the Designated Body misses its 10-day deadline).
Second-level review is conducted by SEBI directly with the Designated Body/entity.

At any point, the investor may instead opt for Online Dispute Resolution (conciliation, then arbitration if conciliation fails) via smartodr.in. Opting for ODR automatically closes the SCORES complaint as disposed.

documents_required: Proof supporting the complaint (contract notes, statements, correspondence, etc. as applicable)
online_process: Entire process is online via SCORES web portal or mobile app.
offline_process: Nearest Investor Service Centre (ISC) of NSE/BSE can assist, particularly with the ODR route.
fees: None mentioned in the source FAQ for filing on SCORES.

expected_timeline.stage: Investor review window after each ATR
Limitation period to file the original complaint from cause of action

rejection_reasons: Complaint not pertaining to investment in the securities market
Anonymous, incomplete, or unspecific complaints; allegations without supporting documents
Against a company on the Dissemination Board, or under liquidation/resolution/struck-off from RoC
Concerns unclaimed dividends/shares/matured debentures already transferred to IEPF (>7 years unclaimed) — must go directly to the IEPF Authority, outside SEBI's purview
Matter already pending or concluded via the ODR mechanism
Complaint is essentially market intelligence (insider trading, price manipulation tips) rather than a personal grievance — route to miportal.sebi.gov.in instead
next_step_if_rejected: If SCORES disposes the complaint unsatisfactorily: pursue Online Dispute Resolution (smartodr.in), consumer courts, or other civil remedies.

If the complaint is out of SEBI's jurisdiction per the exclusion list, it is routed to the correct authority (RBI/Banking Ombudsman, MCA, IRDAI, PFRDA, CCI, NHB, IBBI, IEPF Authority, or the relevant stock exchange for suspended companies) — see jurisdiction table below.
exchange_channel: NSE/BSE act as Designated Bodies for first-level review in many categories; also operate Investor Service Centres
legal_basis: SEBI Master Circular SEBI/HO/OIAE/OIAE_IAD-1/P/CIR/2023/145 dated July 31, 2023 (Online Dispute Resolution)
SEBI circular SEBI/HO/OIAE/IGRD/CIR/P/2023/156 dated September 20, 2023 (SCORES authentication for Designated Bodies; ODR-SCORES interplay)
Section 125, Companies Act 2013 (unclaimed dividends/shares transfer to IEPF after 7 years — cited as the basis for SCORES excluding IEPF-eligible claims)
confidence_note: step_by_step_process, expected_timeline, rejection_reasons, and legal_basis are extracted verbatim/near-verbatim from scores.sebi.gov.in/faqs, a live Tier-1 SEBI source, crawled and hashed on 2026-08-25 (see data/json/sebi/scores/). This supersedes the 'must be re-verified' caveat originally noted in 01_SOURCE_INVENTORY.md section B.
